# Release compatibility table

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/release/compat-table.mjs --write` from design/compatibility/seed.json and release.packages.json; do not edit. -->

Names are the `target` namespace of release.packages.json (pending [issue 41](https://github.com/baseten/pixi-react/issues/41)). **Tested** means: covered by the PR-tier cells of the [#13 matrix](compatibility/cells/COMPATIBILITY.md), the required check on every pull request. **Verified** means, per render backend (WebGL and WebGPU are checked separately): the tuple's nightly cell passed on that backend in a dated [verification record](compatibility/verification/) whose boundary probes and incompatible pairs all behaved as expected; the exact tuples are `verifiedRanges` in the manifest. Verification is evidence, not a support guarantee, and never widens a peer range (see [release.md](release.md#tested-and-verified)).

**Rendering.** Record [2026-10-11](compatibility/verification/2026-10-11.md): Software rendering: no GPU took part. WebGL ran on ANGLE over SwiftShader and WebGPU on Dawn over SwiftShader's Vulkan device, a fallback adapter (isFallbackAdapter true). It counts as verification; a run on a real GPU (run-cells.mjs --gpu hardware) can be added later as extra evidence. Record [2026-10-11-macos-26-apple-m5-max](compatibility/verification/2026-10-11-macos-26-apple-m5-max.md): Real GPU: ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M5 Max, Unspecified Version); apple / metal-3, isFallbackAdapter false (from adapter.isFallbackAdapter). The render check confirmed no backend ran on a software renderer or a fallback adapter. Record [2026-10-11-windows-26200-nvidia-geforce-rtx-4070-chrome](compatibility/verification/2026-10-11-windows-26200-nvidia-geforce-rtx-4070-chrome.md): Real GPU: ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (0x00002786) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11); nvidia / lovelace, isFallbackAdapter false (from adapter.info.isFallbackAdapter). The render check confirmed no backend ran on a software renderer or a fallback adapter. The browser was Google Chrome 154.0.8037.93 as installed on the machine (Playwright channel chrome), not the Chromium pinned by Playwright.

## The facade

| `@pixi/react` | React peer | React tested | pixi.js peer | pixi.js tested on every PR | pixi.js in the nightly cells | Verified (the adapter packages it builds in) | Builds in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8.1.0 (Release 1, not yet published) | `^19.3.0` | 19.3.0 | `>=8.2.6 <8.5.0 \|\| >=8.5.1 <8.23.0` | 8.2.6, 8.22.0 | 21 versions: the newest audited patch of each minor, 8.2.6 … 8.22.0 | WebGL: React 19.3.0 × pixi.js 8.2.6 … 8.22.0 (21 versions). WebGPU: React 19.3.0 × pixi.js 8.2.6 … 8.9.2 (8 versions)\*, 8.10.2 … 8.22.0 (13 versions) (records [2026-10-11](compatibility/verification/2026-10-11.md), [2026-10-11-macos-26-apple-m5-max](compatibility/verification/2026-10-11-macos-26-apple-m5-max.md), [2026-10-11-windows-26200-nvidia-geforce-rtx-4070-chrome](compatibility/verification/2026-10-11-windows-26200-nvidia-geforce-rtx-4070-chrome.md)) | `@pixi/react-19.3` 8.1.0, `@pixi/react-pixi-8` 8.1.0; react-reconciler 0.34.0, its-fine 2.1.1 |
| 8.0.5 (upstream, for comparison) | `>=19.0.0` | - | `^8.2.6` | - | - | - | react-reconciler 0.31.0 (the React 19.0 epoch), its-fine ^2.0.0 |

\* WebGPU on pixi.js <8.10 needs the workaround for [pixijs/pixijs#11389](https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/issues/11389) (fixed in 8.10.0): without it, WebGPU renders a blank canvas on devices whose WebGL texture-unit count exceeds their WebGPU per-stage limit. Use pixi.js 8.10+ or WebGL. The verification runs apply that workaround as the labelled environment shim `pixi-webgpu-texture-units` (`adapterMatrix.environmentShims`).

On a React 19 minor other than 19.3 the facade installs (its peer is a caret range), runs and logs one warning; pixi.js 8.5.0 is excluded from the range.

\* WebGPU on pixi.js <8.10 needs the workaround for [pixijs/pixijs#11389](https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/issues/11389) (fixed in 8.10.0): without it, WebGPU renders a blank canvas on devices whose WebGL texture-unit count exceeds their WebGPU per-stage limit. Use pixi.js 8.10+ or WebGL. The verification runs apply that workaround as the labelled environment shim `pixi-webgpu-texture-units` (`adapterMatrix.environmentShims`).

Every package releases at the facade's version (8.1.0), and a dependency between our packages names exactly that version: install all `@pixi/react-*` packages at the same version (see [release.md](release.md#lockstep-versions)).

`@pixi/react-pixi-7` targets pixi.js `>=7.2.0 <7.4.0 \|\| >=7.4.2 <7.5.0` but releases at the facade's version like every package; the facade itself composes the default Pixi adapter and stays on its Pixi major.
